overview: This Senate resolution names September 2026 "National Literacy Month." It points to national test results showing weak student reading skills and an estimate that 28 percent of U.S. adults, about 59 million people, read at the lowest proficiency level. It highlights the "science of reading," a body of research behind teaching methods such as phonics (connecting letters to sounds), fluency, vocabulary and comprehension. It calls on governments, schools, libraries, nonprofits, businesses and the public to mark the month with programs and activities. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say low literacy holds back millions of people and costs the economy dearly, so drawing national attention to proven reading instruction is worthwhile.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it changes no law and provides no money for reading programs.
